{{Tooltip|W|Won}} 72–69 vs. [[2021–22 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] }} {{2021–22 Big 12 men's basketball standings}} The '''2021–22 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kansas]] in the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], which was the Jayhawks' 124th basketball season. The Jayhawks, members of the [[Big 12 Conference]], played their home games at [[Allen Fieldhouse]] in [[Lawrence, Kansas]]. They were led by 19th year [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] head coach [[Bill Self]]. The Jayhawks finished the season 34–6 and won their 4th NCAA Tournament National Championship, their first since [[2008 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|2008]], and their 6th National Championship overall. ==Season notes== The Jayhawks experienced massive roster turnover in the offseason having lost eight players to transfers, graduation, and entering the draft, but added a recruiting class ranked in the top 15 of every major recruiting website, and 4 transfers. They had more new players on their roster than returning players. Despite the turnover, the Jayhawks entered the season with high expectations. [[Joe Lunardi]] of [[ESPN]] projected them as a 1 seed in his initial [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]] bracketology.{{cite web |title=Bracketology |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/feature/story/_/page/bracketology/ncaa-bracketology-projecting-2022-march-madness-men-field |website=ESPN.com}} The Jayhawks renewed [[Border War (Kansas–Missouri rivalry)|their rivalry with Missouri]] on December 11. The Jayhawks defeated [[2021–22 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] 102–65.{{cite web |title=Kansas Athletics Announces Border Showdown Rivalry Postponed to 2021-22 Season |url=https://kuathletics.com/kansas-athletics-announces-border-showdown-rivalry-adjustment-due-to-covid-19/ |website=KUAthletics.com|date=October 13, 2020 }} On April 2, 2021, Kansas signed Self to a lifetime contract. The contract will automatically add an extra year to every year he coaches until his retirement or death.{{cite web |title=Kansas Signs Coach Bill Self to Lifetime Contract |url=https://www.si.com/college/2021/04/02/bill-self-kansas-lifetime-contract |website=SI.com|date=April 2, 2021 }} On October 14, 2021, when the Big 12 Preseason Media Poll was published, Kansas was projected to finish first in conference standings, which is the 19th time in 26 seasons of the Big 12's existence that the Jayhawks have been selected as the preseason favorite. They received 8 first-place votes and 80 total points.{{Cite web|last=Tait|first=Matt|date=2021-10-14|title=Kansas basketball picked by Big 12 coaches as preseason favorite|url=https://m.kusports.com/news/2021/oct/14/kansas-basketball-picked-big-12-coaches-2021-22-pr/|access-date=2021-10-15|website=KUsports.com|language=en}} The [[Associated Press]] (AP) released their preseason poll on October 18, 2021. The Jayhawks were ranked 3rd in the preseason poll. It was the 10th consecutive, 16th under Bill Self, and 24th time since the 1992–93 season KU was ranked 7th or higher in the preseason AP poll. It was also the 16th consecutive season KU was ranked in the preseason poll. It also marked KU being ranked in the preseason poll 31 of the previous 32 seasons.{{cite web |title=Kansas No. 3 in Preseason Associated Press Poll |url=https://kuathletics.com/kansas-no-3-in-preseason-associated-press-poll/ |website=KUAthletics.com|date=October 18, 2021 }} After losing to Baylor on February 26 and TCU on March 1, the Jayhawks lost back-to-back games, which is only the 12th losing streak of any length under Self. The Jayhawks defeated Texas on March 5 to clinch their 63rd regular season conference title, extending their NCAA record. It was also their 20th Big 12 title. It was also the 16th Big 12 title in the previous 18 seasons. The Jayhawks would also win the [[2022 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|2022 Big 12 tournament]] to earn their 50th NCAA Tournament appearance and their NCAA record extending 32nd consecutive. The tournament title was the Jayhawks 12th Big 12 Tournament title and their 16th overall. After defeating Providence in the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], Kansas passed Kentucky to be the winningest program in the nation.{{cite web |title=Martin scores 23, top-seeded Kansas beats Providence 66-61 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401408627 |website=ESPN.com}} The Jayhawks defeated North Carolina in the [[2022 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|National Championship game]] 72–69 after trailing 40–25 at halftime. They trailed by as much as 16 completing the largest comeback in National Championship game history.{{cite web |title=Jayhawks rally, rock North Carolina 72-69 to win NCAA title |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401408636 |website=ESPN.com}} ==Roster changes== ===Coaching staff changes=== {| class="wikitable" !
